title: Quiet Knee
intro: Slow, controlled loading of the leg suits a sore knee, Achilles or ankle, so one session covers all three. If only one is sore, the session still fits. The balance work matters most if you've sprained that ankle before.

Leave at least 48 hours between sessions. Don't do it the day after braking or change-of-direction work on court, or the day before a match, or when the leg is still hammered from something else. Wherever it hurts, find the depth or step height where it stays quiet and work there, because the position that hurts is the wrong position. You need a wall or a rail and a low step. Nothing here jumps. The Wall Sit is fine on its own before you play, as two holds at an RPE of 6 instead of four. If it's no better after about six weeks, see a physio, or sooner if it's getting worse or coming on earlier than it used to.

before.label: Who it's for
before.text: A sore knee, Achilles or ankle that a doctor or physio has already looked at and cleared you to train.

before.label: Stop and get it looked at
before.text: A snap or a pop and you lost your push-off, the knee gives way, locks or keeps swelling, you can't put your full weight on it, it swelled up fast after a twist or a landing, or one calf is swollen, warm or tender and you didn't strain it playing. That last one needs a doctor the same day.

before.label: While you train
before.text: A bit of ache is fine. Sharp pain isn't, and neither is pain that builds through a set or feels worse the next morning. If it builds, stop that exercise. If it's sharp, stop the session. On a flared-up day, do just the Wall Sit block at an RPE of 6 and don't mark the session done.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.note: Let pain set the depth, and if it feels easier than a 7 at a depth that stays quiet, hold it for the full time anyway.

exercises.name: Lateral Step-Down
exercises.note: If your knee, Achilles or ankle feels worse the next morning than before you started, drop one set from each exercise in this block next time, and if it's still worse after that, get it looked at.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.note: Once the bodyweight version feels easier than a 7, hold something heavy in the other hand and add weight before you add reps.
